question: Who gave M. K. Gandhi a title of Mahatma?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The title **"Mahatma"** means "Great Soul" in Sanskrit.
 
• It was first used by **Rabindranath Tagore**, the famous Bengali poet, to describe **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• The term was not officially given to Gandhi at the time, but Tagore used it as a tribute to Gandhi’s moral and spiritual stature, particularly about his leadership in the Indian independence struggle and his commitment to non-violence (ahimsa) and truth (satyagraha).
 
• Gandhi's simple lifestyle, deep spirituality, and his focus on the welfare of the common people made him a revered figure, deserving of such a title in Tagore’s eyes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lokmanya Tilak**: Known for his slogan "Swaraj is my birthright," Tilak was a prominent freedom fighter and a contemporary of Gandhi, but he did not give Gandhi the title of "Mahatma." Tilak was more known for his fiery nationalism and his leadership in the early stages of India's struggle for independence.
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**: Gokhale was one of Gandhi’s early mentors, but he did not give Gandhi the title "Mahatma." Gokhale was known for his moderate approach towards British rule and his focus on social reform.
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**: Dadabhai Naoroji, an important leader of the Indian National Congress and the first Asian to be a British Member of Parliament, was another influential figure in India's independence movement. He did not use the term "Mahatma" for Gandhi either.
